title: Keep telemetry vendor SDK imports out of core layers

facts.note: File path carries a layer segment other than integration. Integration-layer files and unlayered entrypoints (composition root, scripts) are out of scope.
Paths under an infrastructure/ directory are the adapter location and exempt.

values: file contains an import (value or type-only) of a vendor_sdk package
facts.note: Needs an import-level observer matching the vendor_sdk package list against the file's current imports — covers pre-existing imports, newly added imports, and files newly moved into a prohibited layer, not only added lines.

fires: A domain-layer file contains `import { trace } from "@opentelemetry/api"` to emit a span directly.
An application-layer file contains `import type { Scope } from "@sentry/node"` (type-only still counts).
A presentation-layer file imports `mixpanel` or `@amplitude/analytics-browser` to track an event.
A file that already imports `dd-trace` is moved from integration/ into an assembly-layer path.
doesNotFire: An integration-layer file imports `@opentelemetry/api` to implement the TelemetryPort adapter.
A file under an infrastructure/ directory imports `@sentry/node`.
An unlayered composition root or script imports a vendor SDK to wire adapters.
A domain file imports only the neutral TelemetryPort type.
The repository has not adopted this rule family (rule is inert).

given: A layered source file (domain, application, presentation, assembly) not under an infrastructure/ directory
when: it imports (value or type-only) a telemetry vendor SDK: @opentelemetry/*, @sentry/*, @datadog/*, dd-trace, newrelic, segment (bare or @segment/*), mixpanel (bare or @mixpanel/*), amplitude (bare or @amplitude/*), @posthog/*, @statsig/*, @braze/*, @heap/*, @rudderstack/*
then: The file MUST NOT import a telemetry vendor SDK.
prefer: Depend on the port; adapt at the edge: core takes a TelemetryPort parameter, e.g. in domain/: `export function acceptResponse(response, telemetry: TelemetryPort) { telemetry.emit(...); }` — no SDK.
Put the SDK in an adapter under infrastructure/ or the integration layer, e.g. infrastructure/otel-adapter.ts: `import { metrics } from "@opentelemetry/api";` — the SDK lives there and only there.
avoid: Type-only vendor imports in core: the coupling is real even when erased.
Relabelling or moving a file just to escape the check instead of splitting port and adapter.
unless: Integration layer or infrastructure/ path: exempt by design, the adapter belongs there.
Unlayered entrypoints (composition root, script): outside this rule — they wire adapters, they do not become one.
Inert until adoption, like every rule in this family.
why: Core depends only on a TelemetryPort; once a domain module imports an exporter, every module behind it inherits the vendor and exporter-neutrality is gone.
evidence: The bun_telemetry_code validator reports no finding for layered files outside integration/ and infrastructure/.
Review: no value or type-only vendor_sdk import exists in domain, application, presentation or assembly files outside infrastructure/.
Core telemetry emission goes through a TelemetryPort dependency; the SDK appears only in an integration-layer or infrastructure/ adapter.
verifier_detail: vendor_sdk package matchers: @opentelemetry/*, @sentry/*, @datadog/*, dd-trace, newrelic, segment (bare or @segment/*), mixpanel (bare or @mixpanel/*), amplitude (bare or @amplitude/*), @posthog/*, @statsig/*, @braze/*, @heap/*, @rudderstack/*.

Scope: files whose path carries a layer segment (domain, application, presentation, integration, assembly). A vendor SDK import is allowed only when the layer is integration or the path sits under infrastructure/.
adapter_location = the integration layer, or an infrastructure/ directory — the outer ring where exporters are wired to the neutral TelemetryPort.
Unlayered files (no layer segment, e.g. composition root, scripts) are not checked.
Rule is inert until the repository adopts it (family-wide adoption gate).
Implemented by validator ref bun_telemetry_code; severity 2; disposition strict.
audit: original name: Telemetry vendor SDKs stay in infrastructure adapters
original summary wording: 'every wagon behind it inherits the vendor, and the plan's exporter-neutrality promise is gone'

sharedNodes.text: Disposition strict: the checker fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

Layer segments: domain, application, presentation, integration, assembly. The integration layer and infrastructure/ directories form the outer ring where adapters wire external SDKs to neutral ports; core layers depend only on ports. Unlayered entrypoints (composition root, scripts) wire adapters.

additions.text: Relabelling or moving a file just to escape the check instead of splitting port and adapter.
additions.justification: Metric-gaming anti-pattern required by the author format; not present in the source.

additions.text: Concrete fires/doesNotFire examples using vendor package names from the source list.
additions.justification: Activation examples are required; they only instantiate source-listed packages and layers.

additions.text: None: the source has a single obligation (the import prohibition); port substitution and adapter placement are remediation in prefer.
Length note: coder-facing text exceeds the ~1,000-char target because the complete vendor_sdk package list is repeated in `when` so the coder sees the exact package boundary.
